They walk from the doorway toward open ground
a.explanation: The doorway is behind animals and people moving down to the land.

a.prompt: Did the people just arrive to board, or have they already left? Which clue helps?
options: They are boarding: they face the doorway
They have left: the ark is behind them
They are waiting inside beside the door
a.explanation: They stand in the open with the side of the ark behind them.

a.prompt: More animals are near the doorway. Why can they follow the people this time?
options: There is ground all the way from the ark to the family
Only the top of a tree is above the water
There is water between the family and the ark
a.explanation: Animals and people now share one continuous stretch of land.

b.prompt: What do you see beyond this doorway that a mountaintop above water could not guarantee?
options: That every animal has already left the ark
A stretch of dry land the group can walk onto
That the door has been open since the rain stopped
b.explanation: The land stretches directly out from the doorway. A lone peak gave no such route.

b.prompt: Which two details together make this departure different from the earlier boarding?
options: The people face the land and the doorway is behind them
The sheep are together and the ark is wooden
There are people of different ages and animals
b.explanation: The same people and animals can appear in both scenes. Their direction from the door settles it.

b.prompt: Could this group already have been on land when the ark first touched a mountain? Compare the two scenes.
options: Here the family is boarding; on the mountain they had just set out
Both pictures show people leaving as soon as a peak appears
Here the people stand outside; on the mountain they still waited aboard
b.explanation: A resting ark was an earlier sign. The group with the ark behind it represents departure after the ground dried.

b.prompt: The family stands outside and animals follow. Which event from earlier in Noah’s story does this gathering answer most directly?
options: The dove crossed the water alone and came back to Noah
The same household and animals once gathered to enter
A supply of grain was carried in before the journey
b.explanation: Both scenes show the household and the creatures together. The earlier one brings them in; this one takes them out.

teen.prompt: Would dry ground beyond the open door explain the departure on its own in Genesis 8?
options: It shows that Noah left as soon as the dove returned
It shows that God spoke only after everyone had left
It explains how they can leave; God’s command explains why they leave now
teen.explanation: The physical condition and the spoken instruction are separate steps in the account.

teen.prompt: The sheep move out alongside the people. Which part of the command is shown, and which part is still a future purpose?
options: Their multiplication is pictured; bringing them out still lies ahead
Bringing the animals out is pictured; their multiplication on earth still lies ahead
Their entry in pairs is pictured; their stay in the ark still lies ahead
teen.explanation: Genesis 8:17 links disembarking with the future flourishing of life on land.

teen.prompt: People face away from the ark. What does that reversal of direction help explain about the ark’s role?
options: Its work as a temporary refuge has been fulfilled
The household must divide into those who stay and those who leave
The ark will take the animals away on its own
teen.explanation: The same family once moved into shelter. In the new scene the ark is behind them.

teen.prompt: Compare this family gathering with the earlier gathering at the entrance. Which difference is most precise?
options: The household is together again, still approaching the ark for shelter
The household is together again, but the animals have stayed aboard
The household is together again, but now the ark is behind it
teen.explanation: The group’s position and the animals outside make this the counterpart to boarding.

c.prompt: The doorway holds darkness inside and sunlit ground outside. Which narrative boundary can that visual contrast suggest without collapsing two moments?
options: Dry ground makes departure possible; the command initiates it
The first sight of ground is already the instruction to depart
The arrival of a leaf and the actual departure are simultaneous
c.explanation: Genesis narrates the drying of the ground and then gives direct speech instructing Noah to leave.

c.prompt: Sheep and household members share a route from the ark. How does this grouping connect two imperatives given to Noah at different times?
options: The duty to gather provisions is repeated outside in identical terms
The command to build is repeated as a command to dismantle the ark
The living creatures once brought in are now to be brought out
c.explanation: Bringing living creatures aboard preserves them through danger; bringing them out restores life to the land.

c.prompt: What makes the position of the family in front of the ark a counterpart to the earlier entry account, beyond the repeated setting?
options: The household receives the same command to enter the shelter
The household crosses the same boundary in the opposite direction
The household waits outside while only the creatures cross the boundary
c.explanation: The scriptural accounts name the household at both entry and departure. The ark behind the family makes the reversal visible.

c.prompt: A viewer sees the household on land with the ark behind it. Which distinction between reported obedience and initiative requires the text?
options: Departure follows a command; building the altar follows without a new command
Building the altar precedes the command that makes departure possible
The family’s departure and the sacrifice are one commanded act
c.explanation: The outdoor gathering can represent the departure. The sequence of speech, compliance and altar appears in Genesis 8:15–20.

a.prompt: Has all the water vanished? Look under the colored sky as well as up at it.
options: Yes. Every patch of ground is dusty
No. Deep water still covers every hill
No. Small pools remain on the land
a.explanation: A pool catches the light under the bow, with grass and hills around it.

a.prompt: Noah held out his hand to the dove before. What is his raised hand doing this time?
options: To welcome the dove at the window
To show the family something in the sky
To guide the sheep up the ramp
a.explanation: The family stands outdoors looking up. Noah’s hand directs them to the colors in the sky.

a.prompt: Is this promise only for the people? Who else in the picture gives you a clue?
options: The sheep beside the family are included too
Only the person pointing is included
Only the people nearest the ark are included
a.explanation: The story includes the animals in the promise. Here they stand beside the family.

a.prompt: The ark and the bow are both here. Which helped the family then, and which reminds them of a promise now?
options: The bow kept them safe; the ark reminds them now
They had to get inside both to stay safe
The ark kept them safe; the bow reminds them now
a.explanation: The ark in the distance was their shelter in the flood. The bow overhead comes later in their story.

b.prompt: The bow appears while clouds and pools of water are still visible. Which reading fits all three?
options: The sign can appear while traces of rain remain
The sign must wait until all water has vanished
The sign means that the ark is floating again
b.explanation: The remaining water and clouds fit the sign of a promise about a destructive flood, not a promise of endless dry weather.

b.prompt: Noah points up while others look. What can his gesture tell a viewer who has not heard the promise?
options: The exact words God said to Noah
How many years the promise will last
Which part of the scene the family is noticing
b.explanation: The gesture draws attention to the sky. Its meaning as a covenant comes from the story.

b.prompt: Suppose the artist painted only Noah’s family under the bow. Which part of the story would the sheep in this picture help restore?
options: Each animal is meant to receive a separate sign
The promise also includes living creatures besides people
Only the creatures standing close to Noah share the promise
b.explanation: Genesis names both people and living creatures. Showing animals beside the family gives that second group a place in the scene.

b.prompt: Compare the distant ark and the bow over it. Which tells of the family’s past and which points to the future?
options: The ark recalls shelter; the bow recalls the promise
The ark stands for future rain; the bow recalls loading food
The ark and the bow both mark the moment of boarding
b.explanation: The ark sheltered the family during the flood. The bow is the sign given afterward.

teen.prompt: The sign is set in clouds above a wet landscape. Which limit on the promise do these two details help clarify?
options: It protects only the land that already looks dry
It concerns destruction by flood, not the disappearance of rain
It ends whenever moisture forms in the clouds
teen.explanation: Genesis places the bow within the clouds while promising against another flood of that scope.

teen.prompt: The family looks where Noah points. Which part of the covenant cannot be read from that human gesture?
options: Who promises to remember on seeing the bow
Which way the person pointing is facing
Which part of the landscape draws the group’s gaze
teen.explanation: The raised hand guides the human gaze. Genesis 9 gives the promise of remembrance to God.

teen.prompt: The scene includes one family and animals. Which words stretch the covenant beyond this group?
options: “Noah and his sons with him”
“All that came out of the ark”
“Your descendants after you”
teen.explanation: The descendants need not stand beside Noah to be included in the covenant.

teen.prompt: An artist could have left the ark out of this rainbow scene. What link between chapters would that remove from the picture?
options: The very same object both sheltered the family and serves as the covenant sign
The site of earlier rescue remains visible beside the sign of a future promise
The covenant sign had to be seen from inside the ark before anyone could leave
teen.explanation: The two objects connect successive episodes. Each plays its own role in the text.

c.prompt: The bow stands in a cloud above ground where water still glistens. Which reading can account for both details and Genesis 9:13–15?
options: The bow appears only when moisture has vanished from the land
The covenant holds only for the duration of a visible rainbow
Clouds can return; the covenant limits what their waters will destroy
c.explanation: The passage anticipates the gathering of clouds and ties remembrance to the bow appearing in them.

c.prompt: The artist shows a pointing figure and people looking. Where does the biblical account of seeing and remembering put the emphasis instead?
options: Noah sees the sign and renews the covenant by pointing it out
God sees the sign and remembers the everlasting covenant
The household sees the sign and promises to remember the flood
c.explanation: The gesture is a pictorial interpretation. In 9:16 God says that he will see the bow and remember.

c.prompt: A family and sheep share the ground under the bow. Which extension of the covenant can this group illustrate, and which still exceeds the frame?
options: Animals as recipients are visible; future generations are not
Future generations are visible; present creatures are only implied
The pictured family marks both the beginning and the limit of the covenant
c.explanation: Shared ground gives form to the inclusion of creatures. The temporal reach has to be supplied from the words of the covenant.

c.prompt: Read the distant ark and the bow as signs of two different relationships to danger. Which comparison fits their narrative functions?
options: The ark guaranteed no further flood; the bow protected the family while afloat
Both guarantee escape from each new flood to those who seek shelter in the ark
The ark preserved lives during one disaster; the bow marks a promise about future ones
c.explanation: The ark serves as shelter in the narrated flood. The bow is the sign of the promise against another flood destroying all flesh.
